selection: second round after a failed sweep test

neighbours.label: The dash that closes a gerund comparison ('Doing X is like doing Y –'), just before the writer expands on it; the same dash without a comparison stays quiet
fire: Finding a flat is a lot like hunting for treasure – most days you find nothing.
Learning a language is like building a house – you start with the foundations.
Managing a team is rather like cooking for a crowd – someone always complains.
Buying a used car is like playing poker – never show your hand.
Writing a novel is much like running a marathon – the middle miles are the worst.
Growing tomatoes is like raising children – they need patience and water.
Editing a film is just like solving a puzzle – every piece has to fit.
Moving abroad is a bit like starting school again – you know nobody at first.
quiet: Finding a flat takes a lot of time and money – most days you find nothing.
Learning a language takes several years of practice – you start with the basics.
Managing a team requires clear rules and habits – someone always complains.
Buying a used car involves a lot of paperwork – never skip the checks.
Writing a novel takes about two years for me – the middle chapters are the worst.
Growing tomatoes needs a warm and sunny spot – they need patience and water.
Editing a film takes many weeks of careful work – every piece has to fit.
Moving abroad costs a lot more than I thought – you know nobody at first.

notes: Second round. My first test (punctuation closing a 'like' simile, in the sweep with seed 202611051801) failed at AUROC 0.859: dashes after a simile scored 0.38-0.43, periods mostly 0.10-0.17. Probe of this narrower label: 'like herding cats –' 0.32, 'like driving at night –' 0.31; but noun comparands were weaker ('like a family –' 0.10, 'tastes like my mother's –' 0.07), so the test uses gerund comparands only. Dash without a comparison 0.02-0.17.
